# Execution Toolkit

The bridge from an approved strategy to activity on the ground: a self-contained pack any team, market or partner can run to the same standard, without the strategist in the room.

**6 of 10 assets still to be produced.** They are listed as such rather than implied to exist.

**Not approved.** The assets and the do-not-say lines are a person's to approve, and no owner has.

## A · The strategic foundation

**Platform recap.** Execute an earned-led, proof-first Vivacom reputation programme that makes the value people already rely on visible, useful and believable. The final platform line is not locked, so this toolkit operationalises the shared ground across the three candidates: do not ask audiences to forget the bumpy road; show reviewed proof through everyday Bulgarian life; build warmth only where it can be evidenced.

**Story skeleton.** Insight: People do not give a telecom warmth just because it lists achievements, especially when they remember integrations, migrations, service frustrations and old-incumbent residue. · Reason to Believe: Vivacom has usable proof across fibre, EON, 5G, 10-gigabit capability, awards, CSR, skills programmes, customer-use stories and city or household relevance, provided every major claim is reviewed, sourced and paired with a human consequence. · Benefit: Customers, media, employees and critical urban audiences can understand Vivacom as more useful, modern and personally relevant in daily life, not merely bigger or louder. · Proof: The programme runs through a claim-plus-proof hub, customer validation, earned-led newsroom activity, innovation briefings, owned explainers, shared human formats and selective paid amplification.

**Strategy recap.** Sequence proof before emotion: choose and validate the platform route, build the claim-plus-proof architecture, align leaders and Legal/Regulatory, test the story first with existing customers, then scale through earned-led reputation moments supported by owned proof, shared translation and paid amplification. Always-on conversation management and the Observatory newsroom hold the baseline between signature moments.

## B · The plan

### Pre-Seed / Tease

**Objective.** Create the operating foundation before external scale: lock the route, review claims, prepare leadership, establish customer validation and build the proof base.

**Audience.** Leadership, Corporate Communications, Legal, Regulatory Affairs, employees and selected existing-customer validation groups.

**Messages.** A warmer Vivacom must also be a more disciplined Vivacom. · Every major claim needs proof, ownership and review before it becomes a reputation asset. · Existing customers are the first-believer audience; the story must feel true to them before it scales.

**Activities.** Complete route decision between the open platform candidates. · Build the Claim-Plus-Proof Hub. · Prepare spokesperson narrative and red-line guidance. · Design customer validation for the Stayed With Vivacom Proof Series. · Prepare town hall materials and employee alignment.

### Launch

**Objective.** Introduce the proof-led story publicly through credible earned and owned moments while avoiding unsupported warmth or dominance framing.

**Audience.** Existing customers, media, critical urban audiences, employees and technology commentators.

**Messages.** Vivacom is not asking people to forget the bumpy road; it is showing how the value of staying is becoming easier to see. · Vivacom's scale matters when it is experienced as usefulness in everyday Bulgarian life. · Innovation earns reputation value when it shows who benefits.

**Activities.** Publish the first customer proof stories. · Launch owned proof hub content and fact-sheet explainers. · Issue the launch press release after claim review. · Run initial media briefings on innovation with human consequence. · Activate social cutdowns and selective paid boosts only against reviewed proof.

### Sustain

**Objective.** Move from burst communication to a steady reputation rhythm that answers real questions and keeps proof visible in ordinary life.

**Audience.** Existing customers, broader public, critical urban audiences, media, employees and Gen Z as a secondary growth audience pending validation.

### Amplify

**Objective.** Use validated proof, third-party credibility and audience participation to create visible reputation lift at scale.

**Audience.** Professional influencers, sector voices, employees, existing customers, fans and followers.

**Messages.** Vivacom's proof is strongest when credible people can see, use and repeat it themselves. · The company people already rely on is becoming more useful, modern and personally relevant. · Warmth is earned through proof audiences can recognise and defend.

**Activities.** Amplify the strongest earned stories with paid support. · Equip employees and credible third parties with reviewed message materials. · Package reputation proof into event and experiential formats. · Publish recap infographics and imagery from validated proof. · Evaluate pull-through, sentiment quality, proof believability and participation before recalibrating.

### The editorial calendar

## C · The messages & assets

### Message tracks

#### Existing customers who stayed through integrations, migrations and service frustrations

**Insight.** They will not accept warmth unless the communication acknowledges the bumpy road and shows concrete value.

**Benefit.** Staying with Vivacom can feel like a sensible choice, not just inertia.

**Proof.** Customer proof stories, reviewed service and product claims, EON and fibre use cases, validation learnings and owned explainers.

**What they will say.** We know staying through change has not always felt simple. That is why we are showing, with specific proof, how Vivacom now helps your home, work, family and entertainment connect better every day.

**What they will see.** Customer-use stories, practical proof explainers, service reassurance, social cutdowns and invitations to validate or submit everyday moments.

#### Critical urban audiences and broader public

**Insight.** Vivacom's scale helps reputation only when people see what it enables in ordinary life, not when it sounds like dominance.

**Benefit.** They can understand Vivacom as useful infrastructure for modern Bulgarian life without being asked to admire corporate size.

**Proof.** City, household, work, entertainment, education, CSR and skills stories supported by the proof hub.

**What they will say.** Vivacom's scale matters when it is useful: when it helps homes work, families connect, entertainment run, skills grow and communities participate in modern Bulgarian life.

**What they will see.** Everyday Bulgaria Newsroom stories, city and community explainers, human-use imagery, earned articles and social formats.

#### Media, technology commentators and business audiences

**Insight.** Innovation proof has value only when it explains who benefits and what changes for them.

**Benefit.** Coverage can shift from lists of firsts toward credible human and business consequence.

**Proof.** Reviewed proof pairs for 5G, 10-gigabit, EON, awards and business-use examples, with Legal/Regulatory red lines.

**What they will say.** The point of innovation is not the claim itself. The point is what changes for people, homes, businesses and digital life when that capability is available and useful.

**What they will see.** Media briefings, fact sheets, technical explainers, commentator materials and shared cutdowns with clear claim boundaries.

#### Leadership, Corporate Communications, Legal and Regulatory Affairs

**Insight.** Warmer storytelling creates risk unless claims are specific, owned, sourced and reviewable.

**Benefit.** They can align around a story that is emotionally warmer because it is operationally disciplined.

**Proof.** Claim-plus-proof hub, Key-Message Table, red-line guidance, Q&A, spokesperson materials and review workflow.

**What they will say.** A warmer Vivacom cannot be built from softer words alone. It has to be built from claims we can prove, own and review before they reach audiences.

**What they will see.** Claim register, proof pairs, approval notes, leadership narrative, FAQ and town hall cascade materials.

#### Employees and internal advocates

**Insight.** Employees can carry the story credibly if they understand the proof and the boundaries.

**Benefit.** They can explain the company story consistently without overclaiming.

**Proof.** Town hall narrative, spokesperson materials, Q&A, employee-ready proof examples and internal cascade content.

**What they will say.** We are making Vivacom's value easier to see by connecting every claim to real examples from customers, communities, services and everyday life.

**What they will see.** Internal briefings, manager talking points, employee social guidance, Q&A and proof-led story examples.

#### Gen Z audiences

**Insight.** Gen Z is named as a secondary growth audience, but the material does not yet prove which formats or messages will work.

**Benefit.** Vivacom can test relevance in digital, colourful and personally useful formats without pretending validation already exists.

**Proof.** Format tests, social listening, digital-first content pilots and innovation stories translated into practical youth relevance.

**What they will say.** For younger audiences, Vivacom has to show up in ways that feel useful to digital life, and we will test what actually earns attention before scaling it.

**What they will see.** Short-form social tests, visual explainers, digital-life stories and creator-informed formats once validated.

| step | what you do | output |

## Influencer and creator activation

A repeatable way to activate creators, with the targets stated up front rather than negotiated each time.

**Targets, per creator.** 1 blog / long post · 3–5 social updates over ~14 days · 2–3 posts per day during a live challenge · an agreed number of pieces committed up front

**Golden rules.** be relevant & targeted · crowd-source their expertise · personalise — never cut-and-paste · make it easy — ready assets, local adaptation · be transparent and require disclosure of gifted product · be persistent with relevance

## Localisation — global toolkit → local markets

One core toolkit of channel-agnostic assets that local markets adapt. What is fixed and what is flexible is marked here, because a market that is not told will decide for itself.

# Measurement & Evaluation

Start from the business change and work backwards. A metric that cannot be connected upward to an audience change or an organizational objective does not belong here.

**Not approved.** The organizational objective is a person's to approve, and no owner is recorded.

## The AMEC chain

Organizational objectives → Communication objectives → Inputs → Activities → Outputs → Outtakes → Outcomes → Impact.

## Objectives

### Organizational (at most 1)

- by date not established, increase re-seeing Vivacom as indispensable, innovative and personally relevant among existing customers and priority stakeholders from baseline not established to measurable lift in affinity and preference, numeric target not established.

### Communication (at most 3)

- by the next town hall, increase leadership alignment around one proof-led reputation route among Vivacom leadership from baseline not established to one approved route, one legally reviewable claim-plus-proof architecture and one existing-customer validation plan.
- by date not established, increase warmth and pride among existing customers who stayed through integrations, migrations and service frustrations from baseline not established to measurable lift in the feeling that Vivacom is 'my telecom', numeric target not established.
- by date not established, decrease BTK and old state-telecom association among existing customers and critical urban audiences from baseline not established to measurable reduction, numeric target not established.

### Executive KPIs (at most 5)

- by the next town hall, increase major audience-facing claims with approved proof pairs among Vivacom campaign claims from baseline not established to all major claims having Legal/Regulatory-reviewable proof pairs before publication.
- by date not established, increase proof believability among existing customers from baseline not established to measurable lift in tested proof-pair credibility, specificity, relevance and non-overclaim ratings, numeric target not established.
- by date not established, increase approved proof-led message pull-through among earned media and commentator coverage from baseline not established to measurable lift in coverage items containing approved proof, human-benefit context and accurate claim boundaries, numeric target not established.
- by date not established, increase digital relevance among Gen Z from baseline not established to measurable lift in ratings of Vivacom formats as digital, colourful, useful and platform-appropriate, numeric target not established.
- by date not established, increase leadership visibility quality among company events, industry events and social-responsibility topics from leaders holding back to active visible roles that use reviewed proof, stay within red lines and support the chosen route.

## The KPI ladder

Each KPI on its level, with what it climbs to and how strongly it can be attributed.

| KPI | level | climbs to | attribution | baseline | target | source | owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Route and proof architecture alignment | Output | leadership alignment around one proof-led reputation route | medium — say 'contributed to', or anything weaker: 'associated with' | baseline not established | one approved route, one legally reviewable claim-plus-proof architecture and one existing-customer validation plan by the next town hall | approved leadership materials, decision record, claim architecture pack and validation-plan signoff | Elitza Georgieva (Chief Communications Officer), with final sign-off path not fully established |
| Approved claim-plus-proof coverage | Output | all major claims having Legal/Regulatory-reviewable proof pairs before publication | medium — say 'contributed to', or anything weaker: 'associated with' | baseline not established; complete legal claim register is not established | all major audience-facing campaign claims have approved proof pairs before publication | claim-plus-proof hub, legal claim register when established, approval workflow records | Corporate Communications with Legal and Regulatory Affairs review; operating owner not fully established |
| Existing-customer validation completeness | Output | existing-customer validation plan | low — say 'associated with' | baseline not established | sufficient completed sample for existing-customer validation; numeric sample target not established | customer validation survey, research panel records, CRM-permitted recruitment logs if access is approved | Elitza Georgieva (Chief Communications Officer); research operations owner not established |
| Proof believability score | Outtake | proof believability among existing customers | medium — say 'contributed to', or anything weaker: 'associated with' | baseline not established | measurable lift in proof believability; numeric target not established | existing-customer validation survey, message testing, qualitative customer interviews | Elitza Georgieva (Chief Communications Officer); research vendor or analytics owner not established |
| Existing-customer warmth and pride | Outcome | warmth and pride among existing customers who stayed | medium — say 'contributed to', or anything weaker: 'associated with' | baseline not established | measurable lift in warmth and pride; numeric target not established | brand tracker, existing-customer validation survey, customer pulse research | Elitza Georgieva (Chief Communications Officer); measurement owner not fully established |
| BTK and old state-telecom association | Outcome | BTK and old state-telecom association among existing customers and critical urban audiences | low — say 'associated with' | baseline not established | measurable reduction in BTK and old state-telecom association; numeric target not established | reputation tracker, association mapping, social listening with human-coded themes, qualitative groups | measurement owner not established |
| Approved proof-led earned pull-through | Outtake | approved proof-led message pull-through among earned media and commentator coverage | low — say 'associated with' | baseline not established | measurable lift in approved proof-led framing and zero unreviewed sensitive claims; numeric target not established | media monitoring corpus, journalist/commentator briefing logs, manual content analysis | Corporate Communications; media monitoring owner not established |
| Leadership visibility quality | Output | leadership visibility quality within sale-process, legal and regulatory constraints | medium — say 'contributed to', or anything weaker: 'associated with' | leaders are holding back because sale and divestment due-diligence processes leave the company without a clearly stated shared strategic vision | active visible roles in company events, industry events and social-responsibility topics within constraints; numeric target not established | spokesperson calendar, event records, speech and post approvals, Legal/Regulatory review notes | Elitza Georgieva (Chief Communications Officer), with Legal/Regulatory review where sensitive claims appear |
| Affinity and preference lift | Impact | organizational objective: re-see Vivacom as indispensable, innovative and personally relevant | low — say 'associated with' | baseline not established | measurable lift in affinity and preference; numeric target not established | reputation tracker, brand tracker, stakeholder survey, customer research | measurement owner not established |
| Gen Z digital relevance | Outtake | digital relevance among Gen Z | low — say 'associated with' | baseline not established | measurable lift in Gen Z digital relevance; numeric target not established | Gen Z message testing, social platform analytics, social listening, youth audience pulse survey | owner not established; likely shared between Corporate Communications and Marketing |

### How each KPI is measured

#### Route and proof architecture alignment

**Definition.** Confirmed approval of one reputation route, one claim-plus-proof architecture and one existing-customer validation plan before the next town hall.

**Collection.** once before the next town hall, then updated when decisions change  ·  **Breakdown.** route choice, claim architecture, validation design, Legal/Regulatory review status, leadership approval status

**Attribution method.** Reported as contributed to by the alignment process when the approval record names the same materials and decision path.  —  correlation with some controls — say 'contributed to'

**Known limitations.** This measures readiness and alignment, not audience perception or business impact.

#### Approved claim-plus-proof coverage

**Definition.** Share of major audience-facing claims that have an approved proof pair, source note, owner and review status before use. Calculation: approved major claims divided by total major audience-facing claims planned or published.

**Collection.** weekly during foundation build; before each publication during activation  ·  **Breakdown.** claim type, audience, channel, proof source, review status, sensitive-claim category, publication status

**Attribution method.** Reported as contributed to by the proof workflow when publication records show the approved proof pair was used.  —  correlation with some controls — say 'contributed to'

**Known limitations.** It confirms discipline in claim use; it does not show whether audiences believed the claims.

#### Existing-customer validation completeness

**Definition.** Whether validation research has enough completed existing-customer responses to read warmth, pride, proof believability and BTK association by the agreed audience cells. Completeness is made of completed responses, required audience-cell coverage and usable exposure data.

**Collection.** at baseline validation, after pilot content and after campaign wave  ·  **Breakdown.** customer tenure, product mix, city, age band, migration experience, exposure group, complaint-history flag if legally and ethically usable

**Attribution method.** Reported as associated with the quality of validation evidence, not as a reputation outcome.  —  directional evidence without controls — say 'associated with', never 'caused'

**Known limitations.** Validation completeness can show whether the test is usable; it is not proof of changed perception.

#### Proof believability score

**Definition.** Share of tested existing customers who rate Vivacom proof pairs positively across four components: specificity, credibility, relevance and non-overclaim. Each component is reported separately and as an aggregate only when all four are collected.

**Collection.** baseline before activation, after pilot content, after campaign wave  ·  **Breakdown.** proof point, message route, customer tenure, city, age band, product relationship, exposure cell, component score

**Attribution method.** Reported as contributed to by the tested proof architecture when matched exposed and unexposed validation cells are available; otherwise reported only as associated.  —  correlation with some controls — say 'contributed to'

**Known limitations.** Believability is an outtake. It does not equal warmth, preference or behaviour.

#### Existing-customer warmth and pride

**Definition.** Change in existing-customer agreement with warmth, pride and 'Vivacom is my telecom' statements, reported as separate statement results and as an aggregate only when all statements are collected.

**Collection.** baseline before activation, mid-campaign pulse, post-campaign readout  ·  **Breakdown.** customer tenure, product bundle, city, age band, migration experience, service-frustration history, content exposure, statement

**Attribution method.** Reported as contributed to by the campaign only where matched comparison or exposure-model evidence is available; otherwise reported as associated with campaign period and exposure.  —  correlation with some controls — say 'contributed to'

**Known limitations.** Service, billing, migration issues, competitor actions and sale-process news can affect warmth and pride.

#### BTK and old state-telecom association

**Definition.** Change in spontaneous or prompted association of Vivacom with BTK, state-telecom legacy, heavy former utility or incumbent dominance.

**Collection.** baseline, mid-campaign pulse, post-campaign, then quarterly if tracker continues  ·  **Breakdown.** audience, city, age band, customer status, message exposure, theme, source type

**Attribution method.** Reported as associated with campaign exposure unless a matched comparison is established; no causal wording from coverage or engagement alone.  —  directional evidence without controls — say 'associated with', never 'caused'

**Known limitations.** Ownership-history news, regulatory debate, duct-network issues and service complaints can move this metric independently.

#### Approved proof-led earned pull-through

**Definition.** Share of relevant earned items that contain all three required components: approved Vivacom proof-led framing, human-benefit context and accurate claim boundaries. Each component is reported separately, and the combined pull-through rate counts only items with all three.

**Collection.** weekly during active earned activity; monthly in always-on periods  ·  **Breakdown.** publication, journalist or commentator type, topic, proof point, message, claim accuracy, tone, correction needed, component present or absent

**Attribution method.** Reported as associated with briefing quality and proof materials unless a controlled media test is used.  —  directional evidence without controls — say 'associated with', never 'caused'

**Known limitations.** Coverage quality is not reach, behaviour or business impact. No monetary equivalence is used.

#### Leadership visibility quality

**Definition.** Count and quality profile of approved leader appearances or statements. Quality is made of four reported components: reviewed proof used, red-line compliance, chosen-route fit and audience relevance. No appearance receives the combined quality label unless all four components are present.

**Collection.** monthly and after each major appearance  ·  **Breakdown.** leader, venue, topic, audience, proof used, approval status, red-line compliance, chosen-route fit, audience relevance, follow-up requests

**Attribution method.** Reported as contributed to by the leadership narrative and review process when approved materials are used in the appearance.  —  correlation with some controls — say 'contributed to'

**Known limitations.** Visibility quality does not establish reputation change without audience research.

#### Affinity and preference lift

**Definition.** Change in Vivacom affinity and preference among existing customers, priority stakeholders and the broader public where measured.

**Collection.** baseline, post-campaign and quarterly if tracker is established  ·  **Breakdown.** audience, customer status, city, age band, stakeholder group, exposure group, message route

**Attribution method.** Reported as associated with campaign activity unless a matched comparison, holdout or approved model is established.  —  directional evidence without controls — say 'associated with', never 'caused'

**Known limitations.** Preference can be affected by price, network experience, service issues, competitor activity and market news.

#### Gen Z digital relevance

**Definition.** Change in Gen Z rating of Vivacom content across four components: digital, colourful, useful and platform-appropriate. Platform interaction quality can support diagnosis only and is reported separately from the perception rating.

**Collection.** after pilot formats, monthly during activation, post-campaign  ·  **Breakdown.** format, platform, topic, age band, creator or channel, exposed versus non-exposed where available, component rating

**Attribution method.** Reported as associated with content exposure unless matched comparison or platform brand-lift design is established.  —  directional evidence without controls — say 'associated with', never 'caused'

**Known limitations.** Positive sentiment or engagement quality is not behaviour or business impact.

## Reporting

**Baseline before launch.** purpose: Establish what is currently known before route choice, proof architecture and external activation. · contents: audience baselines for warmth, pride, BTK association, proof believability, affinity and preference · claim-plus-proof register status and Legal/Regulatory gaps · leadership visibility starting point and constraints · media and social theme baseline without Advertising Value Equivalents and without treating impressions as reach · decisions and next actions: route choice, missing baselines, measurement owner, validation sample and approval path

**During the campaign.** purpose: Track whether the work is staying inside the approved route, proof discipline and audience-learning plan. · contents: claim approval status and unreviewed-claim risks · customer validation reads on believability, warmth and pride · earned message pull-through by required component: approved proof, human-benefit context and accurate claim boundaries · social feedback themes and service-frustration escalations without equating positive sentiment with behaviour or business impact · leadership visibility quality by required component: reviewed proof, red-line compliance, chosen-route fit and audience relevance · decisions and next actions: claims to hold, messages to adjust, proof gaps to close, audiences to retest and issues to escalate

**One-page executive scorecard.** purpose: One-page after-campaign view for leadership. · contents: objective status: met, moving, not moving or not measurable because baseline is missing · KPI table by Output, Outtake, Outcome and Impact · attribution statement using associated with, contributed to or drove only where the method supports it · top risks and limitations, including service, legal, regulatory and sale-process factors · what changed for existing customers, critical urban audiences, Gen Z, media and leadership · decisions and next actions: continue, revise, scale, pause a claim, commission missing research or change ownership

**Cadence.** baseline: once before route choice and before the next town hall pack is locked · during: weekly during foundation and active campaign periods; monthly during always-on reputation activity · post_campaign: one executive scorecard within 2 to 4 weeks after the campaign wave closes, then quarterly reputation tracking if research access is established · rule: Every report ends with decisions and next actions, not observations.

## The three checkpoints

- Measurement gate
- Optimization gate
- Learning gate

## Governance

| role | |
| --- | --- |
| Strategy owner | not yet assigned |
| Measurement lead | not yet assigned |
| Data owner | not yet assigned |
| Account lead | not yet assigned |
| Client sponsor | not yet assigned |
| Quality reviewer | not yet assigned |

## The non-negotiables

These are enforced, not recited.

- Do not use Advertising Value Equivalents
- Do not present impressions as actual reach unless the data supports deduplication
- Do not equate positive sentiment with behaviour or business impact
- Do not aggregate markets without showing material local differences
- Do not optimize solely for the easiest metric to collect
- Always show baseline, target, result and trend together
- Always distinguish what UP delivered, what audiences did, and what changed for the client
- Preserve definitions, query logic and tagging conventions so results are repeatable
- End every report with decisions and next actions, not merely observations

## How an objective is written

`By [date], increase/decrease [audience change] among [specific audience] from [baseline] to [target], contributing to [organizational objective]`

An objective not written this way cannot be measured, because at least one of the date, the change, the audience, the baseline, the target or the business goal is missing.

## The KPI ladder — the template to select from

A fill-in template, not a menu: the operator selects the right KPIs for this campaign. Every campaign carries measures on at least three levels, including one outtake or outcome.

| level | recommended core KPIs | supporting diagnostics |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Outputs | Relevant audience reach; quality coverage rate; key-message penetration | Volume, impressions, publication count, content produced |
| Outtakes | Message recall; understanding; positive consideration; trust/sentiment shift | Engagement rate, video completion, dwell time, comment themes |
| Outcomes | Qualified visits; enquiries; registrations; applications; stakeholder action | CTR, branded search, landing-page behaviour, downloads |
| Impact | Pipeline/revenue contribution; reputation shift; recruitment result; policy/societal progress | Cost per result, efficiency trend, client operational data |

### Quality coverage rate (replaces raw clipping totals)

Score each item against:

- priority outlet/influencer
- priority-audience relevance
- key-message inclusion
- positive or neutral tone
- brand/spokesperson prominence
- desired call to action
- original reporting vs syndication

Report both the percentage meeting the agreed threshold and the underlying criteria. Collapsing them into one unexplained proprietary score is the thing this replaces.

## KPI modules by campaign type

| campaign type | outtake | outcome | impact |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Brand / product | Awareness, recall, message understanding, preference | Branded search, qualified traffic, trials, enquiries, purchases | Sales, market share, customer acquisition, brand-equity change |
| Corporate reputation | Trust, perceived leadership, association with desired attributes | Stakeholder engagement, advocacy, meeting requests, partner interest | Reputation score, licence to operate, risk reduction, investor/partner confidence |
| B2B thought leadership | Decision-maker reach & authoritative coverage. Recognition of expertise & issue understanding | Senior engagement, content consumption, qualified leads, sales conversations | Influenced pipeline and revenue |
| Employer branding | Employer awareness, understanding of EVP, consideration | Career-page visits, qualified applications, offer acceptance | Time-to-hire, cost-per-hire, retention / quality-of-hire |
| Public affairs / public sector | Awareness, understanding, confidence, stakeholder sentiment | Consultation participation, adoption, citizen action, stakeholder support | Policy progress, service uptake, compliance, societal benefit |
| Crisis communications | Response speed, message consistency, stakeholder coverage. Understanding, reassurance, misinformation penetration | Complaint behaviour, stakeholder support, recovery of positive/neutral conversation | Trust recovery, reduced customer loss, risk avoided |

## Reporting cadence

The weekly report must drive action, not simply document activity.

| cadence | what it carries |
| --- | --- |
| Weekly | Five headline KPIs against target, and the action required for each |
| Monthly | The one-page scorecard: objective/KPI, baseline, target, result, status, insight, decision |
| Quarterly | The eight-part evaluation narrative, read against the objectives |

## Open — waiting on a person

- **Is this the organizational objective we are held to?** — not yet approved; no owner recorded.

The format cell is where the volume says what done looks like for each artifact.

12 steps. 12 diverge from their format and 0 did not run in this engagement.

## Where each step stands

| step | verdict | what is missing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 Brief from the Client | diverges from the format | Word document |
| 2 Debrief + elicitation | diverges from the format | Word document format, one-page layout for the Alignment Map table |
| 3 Final Brief | diverges from the format | nothing |
| 4 Research & Analysis | diverges from the format | Structured Word/PDF pack format |
| 5 Frame the Problem → Insights | diverges from the format | Word/PDF card format |
| (opt) Creative Big Idea | diverges from the format | Word/PDF concept format, images, one-sentence strategic summary, the Big Idea |
| 6 Strategic Approach | diverges from the format | chosen strategic approach + one-line positioning |
| 7 Narrative, Messages & Pillars | diverges from the format | Word/PDF format |
| 8 Platform Architecture | diverges from the format | A chosen platform idea, A final judgement of why the chosen platform is ownable, The audience × message × pillar × channel × tactic map, A Word/PDF artifact format |
| 9 Engagement & Rollout | diverges from the format | Word/PDF toolkit pack, complete 12-month content calendar, calendar dates for every month, calendar entries for Month 7, Month 9, and Month 11, collateral library of produced on-template assets |
| 10 Measurement & Evaluation | diverges from the format | Weekly headline-KPI report with five KPIs vs target, Action required for each of the five weekly headline KPIs, Actual one-page scorecard using Objective/KPI × baseline × target × result × status × insight × decision, Results for the scorecard rows, Statuses for the scorecard rows, Insights for the scorecard rows, Decisions for the scorecard rows, Eight-part evaluation narrative following the scorecard |
| 11 Annual Review & Update | diverges from the format | Word/PDF annual review artifact, what worked/what didn't, recommendations, updated Strategy One-Pager for the coming year, re-approval of the updated Strategy One-Pager |

## Step by step

### 1 Brief from the Client

**Document format.** Word document (6 short audit sections + one-paragraph hypothesis), 3–5 pages.

**What the AI drafts.** Runs the six pre-conversation audits from public sources; assembles a briefing pack on the company, its reputation, its peers and the category; drafts a provisional problem hypothesis and a draft Client Style Note.

**Frameworks & tools.** The desk-audit pass before any conversation: Business audit, Reputation audit, Social & digital audit, Competitive audit, Stakeholder scan, Context scan.

**What this run produced.** The artifact contains six short audit sections and a one-paragraph provisional hypothesis, with extra style-note and open-decision sections. It is presented as Markdown text rather than a Word document, though it states a 3-page length.

**Verdict.** diverges from the format — missing: Word document.

### 2 Debrief + elicitation

**Document format.** Word document: structured debrief notes organised by the eight question sets, plus a one-page Alignment Map table (stakeholder × wants × fears × conflict).

**What the AI drafts.** Tailors the question bank to this client from the Step 1 pack; tracks answers against the eight sets in real time; flags thin or evasive answers for follow-up; drafts the debrief write-up.

**Frameworks & tools.** The eight-set question bank, and the six elicitation techniques.

**What this run produced.** The artifact contains structured debrief notes organised under the eight question sets, with knowns, gaps, and follow-up questions for each. It also includes an Alignment Map table using stakeholder, wants, fears, and conflict columns.

**Verdict.** diverges from the format — missing: Word document format, one-page layout for the Alignment Map table.

### 3 Final Brief

**Document format.** Word/PDF: the one-page brief — Client & context; Organizational objective; Reputation problem/opportunity; Priority audiences; Desired change; Stakeholders & alignment; Constraints & guardrails; Assets & access; Success & measurement.

**What the AI drafts.** Assembles the one-page Client Intake Brief from Steps 1–2; maintains the gap register and flags which required fields are still empty; drafts the Measurement Brief skeleton.

**Frameworks & tools.** The gap register (required field × have it? × source × owner × by when), and the Measurement Brief.

**What this run produced.** The artifact contains a client intake brief with all required brief headings: Client & context; Organizational objective; Reputation problem/opportunity; Priority audiences; Desired change; Stakeholders & alignment; Constraints & guardrails; Assets & access; Success & measurement. It also contains additional sections including Scope & logistics, Gap Register, Measurement Brief, and Approval, so it is not just the one-page brief format owed.

**Verdict.** diverges from the format.

### 4 Research & Analysis

**Document format.** One structured Word/PDF pack (not five disconnected audits): executive summary with each finding's so what; bucket-by-bucket sourced findings; Comms-PESTLE + stakeholder map; the five audits; reputation & trust read.

**What the AI drafts.** Desk research; drafts each of the five audits; SOV & sentiment analysis; theme & word-cloud extraction; persona drafts; PESTLE/regulatory/ESG scans — every finding sourced and dated.

**Frameworks & tools.** Buckets & Questions; Communications-PESTLE (reputation lens); stakeholder mapping on the Power/Interest grid.

**What this run produced.** The artifact contains one structured research pack with an executive summary carrying so what implications, bucket-by-bucket sourced findings, Communications-PESTLE, stakeholder map, five audits, and a reputation and trust audit/read. It is presented as Markdown text rather than as a structured Word/PDF pack.

**Verdict.** diverges from the format — missing: Structured Word/PDF pack format.

### 5 Frame the Problem → Insights

**Document format.** Word/PDF card per insight: the insight (1–2 sentences); type (empirical/intuitive/both); the evidence; the tension; the 5 T's check; the audience it's about; the opportunity it opens.

**What the AI drafts.** Generates many candidate insights from the research; surfaces supporting evidence; runs the So-What ladder, the 5 T's, the traps and the Distinctiveness check; drafts the Killer Insight card.

**Frameworks & tools.** Insight-or-not calibration; empirical + intuitive insight; the 5 T's; the So-What ladder.

**What this run produced.** The artifact contains three insight cards, each carrying the insight, type, evidence, tension, 5 T's check, audience it is about, and opportunity it opens. It is presented as a Markdown dossier with screening and validation notes, not as a Word/PDF card artifact.

**Verdict.** diverges from the format — missing: Word/PDF card format.

### (opt) Creative Big Idea

**Document format.** Word/PDF concept (words + images): the one-sentence strategic summary, the elevated objective, the Big Idea, and the criteria check.

**What the AI drafts.** Drafts the internalised brief; generates result-back visions; runs the four brain-trainers at volume to produce many bold candidate ideas; elevates the objectives; validates each against the criteria.

**Frameworks & tools.** The six steps of the Idea Haus, the four brain-trainers, and the Big Idea Criteria.

**What this run produced.** The artifact contains a text-only creative Big Idea dossier with an elevated objective, three built-out candidate ideas, and criteria checks for each candidate. It explicitly says no Big Idea has been chosen and includes no images or Word/PDF concept treatment.

**Verdict.** diverges from the format — missing: Word/PDF concept format, images, one-sentence strategic summary, the Big Idea.

### 6 Strategic Approach

**Document format.** Word/PDF one-pager: executive summary; business & communication objectives (SMART+I); target audience & persona; the strategic approach + one-line positioning; core narrative & 3–5 key messages; proof points; channel strategy (PESO).

**What the AI drafts.** Drafts SMART+I objectives from the brief; generates several distinct strategic approaches from the insight, each with rationale; checks line-of-sight up and down the cascade.

**Frameworks & tools.** The Strategy Cascade; SMART+I; GET/WHO/TO/BY; the selection criteria.

**What this run produced.** The artifact contains an executive summary, business and communication objectives, audience profiling, narrative, key messages, proof points, and a PESO channel shape. It also includes unresolved route options, a blueprint cascade, timeline, KPIs, budget/risk notes, and states that no strategic approach has been chosen.

**Verdict.** diverges from the format — missing: chosen strategic approach + one-line positioning.

### 7 Narrative, Messages & Pillars

**Document format.** Word/PDF: the narrative (template + trailer + tweet); the Key-Message set by audience with laddered proof and do-not-say lines; the 3–5 pillars mapped to narrative, message and story type.

**What the AI drafts.** Drafts narrative options from the insight & approach using the template; generates key messages by audience with proof; proposes pillars mapped to the narrative; ladders messages; drafts the trailer and tweet.

**Frameworks & tools.** The Narrative Template; 6-type Messaging; the Trident ladder; the Content Strategy Cascade.

**What this run produced.** The artifact contains the narrative in the UP template plus trailer and tweet, a key-message table by audience with laddered proof and do-not-say lines, and four communications pillars traced to the narrative with story types. It is presented as a Markdown message architecture rather than a Word/PDF deliverable.

**Verdict.** diverges from the format — missing: Word/PDF format.

### 8 Platform Architecture

**Document format.** Word/PDF: the platform idea + why it's ownable (five-criteria check); the PESO channel architecture (earned-led); the audience × message × pillar × channel × tactic map; the tactics as Activation Cards.

**What the AI drafts.** Generates candidate platforms and tests them against the five criteria; maps tactics to audiences/messages/pillars; drafts Activation Cards; builds the PESO plan; checks every tactic for line of sight.

**Frameworks & tools.** The five platform criteria; PESO; the Activation Card; the four C's of integrated programming.

**What this run produced.** The artifact contains three candidate platform ideas with five-criteria ownability checks, an earned-led PESO channel architecture, and several tactics written as Activation Cards. It also includes supporting architecture material such as an engagement model, communications plan notes, influencer pyramid, and rollout sequencing.

**Verdict.** diverges from the format — missing: A chosen platform idea, A final judgement of why the chosen platform is ownable, The audience × message × pillar × channel × tactic map, A Word/PDF artifact format.

### 9 Engagement & Rollout

**Document format.** Word/PDF toolkit pack + a 12-month content calendar (date/phase × audience track × moment/hook × key message × asset × channel/KPI) + a collateral library of on-template assets.

**What the AI drafts.** Assembles the toolkit from the approved strategy; drafts the phased plan, calendar, message tracks and every collateral asset from templates; localises drafts; wires in tagging & KPIs; runs the pre-publish checklist.

**Frameworks & tools.** The toolkit anatomy; the phased plan; the editorial calendar; the message tracks; the collateral library.

**What this run produced.** The artifact contains a markdown execution toolkit with a strategic foundation, phased rollout plan, nine-row editorial calendar, audience message tracks, collateral status inventory, and activation guidance. It lists toolkit assets, but marks most as still to be produced.

**Verdict.** diverges from the format — missing: Word/PDF toolkit pack, complete 12-month content calendar, calendar dates for every month, calendar entries for Month 7, Month 9, and Month 11, collateral library of produced on-template assets.

### 10 Measurement & Evaluation

**Document format.** Weekly headline-KPI report (5 KPIs vs target, action required) + a one-page scorecard (Objective/KPI × baseline × target × result × status × insight × decision) followed by the eight-part evaluation narrative.

**What the AI drafts.** Selects KPIs from the vetted set per campaign type; wires tagging/UTM/CRM fields; assembles daily/weekly reports and the executive scorecard; matches attribution wording to the evidence confidence level.

**Frameworks & tools.** The AMEC chain; the vertical rule; the executive scorecard; the non-negotiables.

**What this run produced.** The artifact contains a measurement framework with draft objectives, executive KPIs, a KPI ladder, measurement definitions, reporting cadence, governance gaps and non-negotiables. It mentions weekly reporting, a one-page executive scorecard and quarterly evaluation narrative as expected report types, but does not produce them in the required format.

**Verdict.** diverges from the format — missing: Weekly headline-KPI report with five KPIs vs target, Action required for each of the five weekly headline KPIs, Actual one-page scorecard using Objective/KPI × baseline × target × result × status × insight × decision, Results for the scorecard rows, Statuses for the scorecard rows, Insights for the scorecard rows, Decisions for the scorecard rows, Eight-part evaluation narrative following the scorecard.

### 11 Annual Review & Update

**Document format.** Word/PDF annual review (year-on-year tracker movement; reputation/trust read; say-do gap; what worked/what didn't; recommendations) + the updated Strategy One-Pager for the coming year, re-approved.

**What the AI drafts.** Re-runs the reputation/trust audit and tracker comparison year-on-year; assembles the accumulated learning-library findings; drafts a gap analysis between last year's approach and this year's evidence.

**Frameworks & tools.** The yardsticks; the re-tests; the learning library.

**What this run produced.** The artifact contains a markdown annual review with year-on-year tracker movement stated as unavailable due to missing baselines, a reputation/trust read, and a re-tested say-do gap. It also includes strategic re-tests and a learning library, but says the year-ahead strategic approach is not judged or owner-approved.

**Verdict.** diverges from the format — missing: Word/PDF annual review artifact, what worked/what didn't, recommendations, updated Strategy One-Pager for the coming year, re-approval of the updated Strategy One-Pager.

## Storage

**Required.** Client-facing artifacts live in the client folder on Google Drive, versioned; annual-review learnings are logged to Zoho Learn.

**Actual.** This run wrote to a local artifact directory and to nothing else. No Google Drive folder and no Zoho Learn entry were written.

This divergence is the same for every step and is not a judgement about the work.

# The method behind this work

6 of the CUBE's six faces were exercised, and 3 of the 9 signature plays were used. Everything claimed below is quoted from the work itself.

## The method — the CUBE (six faces)

| face | purpose | signature tools | exercised here |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 Navigation | Read the landscape → strategic imperatives & white space | Comms-PESTLE · competitive audit · stakeholder power/interest map · reputation-creation model | yes |
| 2 Discovery | Turn data into insight, insight into foresight | Insight Pyramid · So What? test · Buckets→Questions · Sweet Spot · Reputation Ladder | yes |
| 3 Strategy | Build the architecture that drives behaviour | Strategy Cascade · SMART+I · Brand Archetype · Narrative Template · 6-type Messaging · PESO | yes |
| 4 Ideation | Creative with discipline | Idea Haus · Impact/Feasibility · K.I.C.K. · Activation Card | yes |
| 5 Engagement | Plan content across channels & time | Content Strategy Cascade · Hero/Hub/Hygiene · Tease→Amplify · Pyramid of Influence · Observatory | yes |
| 6 Measurement | Prove reputation impact, not activity | Output→Outtake→Outcome→Impact · VERITE · Reputation Ladder · Trust Pulse | yes |

### What each face rests on

**Navigation — exercised.** The provisional white space is to reclaim incumbent scale as a human and national advantage without former-utility nostalgia, generic network leadership or political nation-building language.

**Discovery — exercised.** The work has moved beyond a pile of facts into organised implications about audiences, proof, risks and constraints, but it has not reached full Insight because primary perception evidence and baselines are still missing.

**Strategy — exercised.** The communication objective delivers the business outcome by turning Vivacom's existing proof into an aligned, legally defensible reputation route and testing it first with the customers whose belief must shift before broader reputation can credibly move.

**Ideation — exercised.** 30 candidates were written and screened; 3 survived; 3 are put forward as cards. Volume first, then judgment.

**Engagement — exercised.** Every slot ties a moment to a message and a ready asset.

**Measurement — exercised.** Start from the business change and work backwards. A metric that cannot be connected upward to an audience change or an organizational objective does not belong here.

## The IP Library — signature plays

| play | used here | evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reputation Ladder | yes | Insight is a level on a ladder, reached by disciplined questioning — not a lucky thought. |
| VERITE | no | VERITE is not named or evidenced in the work. |
| White Space | yes | The provisional white space is to reclaim incumbent scale as a human and national advantage without former-utility nostalgia, generic network leadership or political nation-building language. |
| Take-a-Stand | no | Take-a-Stand is not named or evidenced in the work. |
| Brand Archetype | no | Brand Archetype is not named or evidenced in the work. |
| KICK | no | KICK is not named or evidenced in the work. |
| Authenticity Continuum | no | Authenticity Continuum is not named or evidenced in the work. |
| Trust Pulse | yes | No primary stakeholder dipstick, survey, trust pulse, social listening or audience segmentation is supplied. |
| Outcome Library | no | Outcome Library is not named or evidenced in the work. |

## The guided flow — 15 steps

| # | step | you end up with |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Capture — brief or conversation | A captured brief |
| 2 | Debrief — interrogate & expand | A sharpened problem statement |
| 3 | Final brief, approved | A locked brief + engagement tier |
| 4 | Research (Navigation + Discovery) | Organised evidence (Buckets filled) |
| 5 | Insight (+ Distinctiveness Gate) | 1–3 human-owned Killer Insights |
| 5B | Validate the insight | Evidence the audience holds the tension |
| 6 | Idea | A creative / narrative platform |
| 7 | Strategic approach | The GET/WHO/TO/BY statement |
| 8 | Narrative | The core corporate narrative |
| 9 | Key messages | Multi-track messaging architecture |
| 10 | Content pillars (Themes) | Hero/Hub/Hygiene themes |
| 11 | Channels | PESO + influence plan |
| 12 | Tactical roadmap | Phased 12-month roadmap + activations |
| 13 | Measurement | Reputation measurement framework |
| 14 | Package & present | The 10-slide deck + approvals |
| 15 | Approve, launch & learn | Signed strategy, launch pack, feedback loop |

## System architecture — the four layers

- **LAYER 1 · INTAKE & ROUTER** — Sizes the engagement; sets tier, governance, AI-status; scales CUBE depth.
- **LAYER 2 · KNOWLEDGE BASE** — UP's IP made retrievable: method, theory, IP library, cases, origination.
- **LAYER 3 · GUIDED PROCESS (the CUBE)** — The self-guiding six-face method, run step by step: ask · AI action · example · artifact · gate.
- **LAYER 4 · QUALITY & DELIVERY** — The mechanisms that guarantee operator-independent quality, plus the learning loop.

## The theory — Economics of Reputation

Every strategy rests on an explicit theory of reputation, encoded as reasoning the engine applies from the first step.

| question | the UP position |
| --- | --- |
| What is reputation? | A dynamic construct — perception + judgement + asset. Fluid, never "solved." |
| Why does it matter? | Digital voice, transparency and scandal have made it a board-level asset. |
| How is it created? | Partnerships (borrow prestige) · Initiatives (awards, innovation, symbolic acts) · Associations (leaders' reputations). Consumers co-create it. |
| How does it create value? | Externally — price premium, lower cost of capital, loyalty. Internally — talent, retention, motivation. |
| How is it measured? | Ranking · Rating · Multiple-Stakeholder (RepTrak / Reputation Quotient). |

## The quality system — how quality is made operator-independent

Because a novice cannot be asked to judge, every judgement is moved into the system as a self-enforcing, evidence-gated, AI-adjudicated procedure. Seven mechanisms do this.

| # | mechanism | how it removes operator judgment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M1 | Constrain to proven patterns | Templates/architectures the operator can't build badly |
| M2 | Self-enforcing evidence gates | The system verifies distinctiveness & won't advance without validation evidence — pass by evidence, not opinion |
| M3 | The Adversarial Review Board | AI personas (competitor, CFO, journalist, GC, audience, activist, employee) attack the strategy; it must survive — senior scrutiny without a senior |
| M4 | RAG on the Outcome Library | Every output scored vs. outcome-proven UP precedents — imports UP's taste |
| M5 | Options, never a blank page | The operator chooses among vetted, scored candidates + a recommendation |
| M6 | Systematic creativity | Generate volume, score ownability/memorability/appropriateness, surface top 3 — raises the creative floor |
| M7 | Mandatory validation | Truth is evidence-gated, not conviction-gated |

## Honest limits

Two things resist full systematization, and naming them is the difference between a credible plan and a sales pitch.

- **Unspoken internal politics.** Perceiving a specific client's unspoken internal politics — the system can force the input but can't perceive what the operator doesn't know to enter.
- **Breakthrough originality.** The engine reliably delivers strong-and-distinctive, occasionally brilliant; the top few percent of genius stays human.

**For this pilot's goal, that is the right trade.** The aim is not occasional superhuman brilliance but that a novice and a veteran produce the same excellent strategy. Consistency at excellent is worth more to the firm than high-variance genius — and it is reachable. The engine raises the floor, refuses to let the obvious pass, forces the choices strategy requires, and leaves the true ceiling to the strategist.

## The knowledge base — five pillars

| pillar | contents |
| --- | --- |
| Method | The CUBE — six faces |
| Theory | The Economics of Reputation — the reasoning foundation |
| IP Library | Signature Plays: Narrative Template · 6-type Messaging · Pyramid of Influence · Content Strategy Cascade · Reputation Ladder · Activation Card · VERITE · White Space · Take-a-Stand · Brand Archetype · Idea Haus · KICK · the Authenticity Continuum, and more |
| Cases | 35+ engagements tagged by CUBE face, sector, tier — and, over time, the Outcome Library of what actually moved reputation |
| Origination | The new-business system: go/no-go scorecard, pitch process, Win/Loss survey |

## What tripped the wire

Escalated to: **not yet — no senior human is recorded.** Until a named person takes this, the work does not proceed past here.

## What the tripwire watches

These are the triggers, whether or not any fired. A report that listed only what fired would leave a reader unable to see what else would have stopped the work.

- litigation — **fired**
- disclosure/MNPI — **fired**
- a deal — **fired**
- restructuring — not present in this work
- life-safety — not present in this work
- a regulatory investigation — not present in this work
- insolvency — not present in this work

## The scope charter

Reputation is ongoing and proactive. The sub-services are episodic and transactional.

| in scope — the engine builds reputation | out of scope — separate sub-services |
| --- | --- |
| Corporate positioning & narrative | Investor relations (earnings, guidance, disclosure) |
| Executive visibility & thought leadership | M&A communications |
| ESG / purpose (with proof discipline) | Restructuring & redundancy |
| Employer brand & talent reputation | Litigation communications |
| Earned media & influence | Public affairs & lobbying |
| Owned digital & social ecosystem |  |
| Internal comms & culture |  |
| Stakeholder relationship-building |  |
| Reputation & trust measurement |  |
| Crisis preparedness & reputation-level response |  |

### Where the work strays

- **M&A communications.** This answers sale/divestment communications, which belongs to M&A communications.
  Quoted: "The sale context is creating strategic silence: leaders are waiting for a sale and piecemeal divestment due diligence, and "nobody dares say anything.""
- **M&A communications.** This frames reputational handling during sale processes, which belongs to M&A communications.

- **Public affairs & lobbying.** This answers regulator and government handling, which belongs to public affairs.
  Quoted: "Boasting about being market leader across segments is discouraged because it invites regulator and government attention."
- **Public affairs & lobbying.** This concerns infrastructure-access pressure and competitor/regulatory positioning, which belongs to public affairs.
  Quoted: "The duct network is an extra-care topic and a competitor attack vector."
- **Public affairs & lobbying.** This answers state and national-security handling, which belongs to public affairs.
  Quoted: "State-layer and national-security handling is flagged and quarantined until confirmed."
- **M&A communications.** Leadership-transition handling is a transaction-sensitive corporate-change topic, which belongs to M&A communications if tied to ownership/sale transition.
  Quoted: "No AI-use or MNPI protocol is supplied beyond the briefing pack's instruction that the leadership transition trigger is excluded from AI use."
- **M&A communications.** This directly answers communications around a possible sale and divestment due diligence.
  Quoted: "The current trigger is a need to define a clearer corporate reputation story while a possible sale process and divestment due diligence are creating strategic silence inside the company."
- **M&A communications.** This defines communications constraints caused by sale and divestment processes.
  Quoted: "The central alignment tension is between Elitza Georgieva's wish for a more emotional, likeable, digital and visible Vivacom and leaders' reluctance to make forward-looking statements while the company is waiting for a sale and piecemeal divestment due diligence."
- **Public affairs & lobbying.** This includes government, regulator, infrastructure and national-security topics, which belong to public affairs.
  Quoted: "Duct network, Recovery and Resilience Plan projects, ownership history, market-leader boasting, state-layer or national-security material, satellite/teleport reach and ownership-transition communications all require extra care."
- **M&A communications.** Ownership-transition communications belong to M&A communications.
  Quoted: "ownership-transition communications all require extra care"
- **Public affairs & lobbying.** This answers government and regulator optics, which belongs to public affairs.
  Quoted: "Government and regulator optics are sensitive because market-leader boasting, duct-network access, Recovery and Resilience Plan projects and ownership-transition communication can draw scrutiny."
- **M&A communications.** Ownership-transition communication belongs to M&A communications.
  Quoted: "ownership-transition communication can draw scrutiny"

## Data and AI

- Material non-public information present: **yes**
- Client restricts AI use: **yes**
- MNPI/sensitive transaction indicators: "possible sale process and divestment due diligence are creating strategic silence inside the company" and "leaders are waiting for a sale and piecemeal divestment due diligence." AI restriction indicator: "the leadership transition trigger is excluded from AI use."

MNPI never enters AI tools. Where a client is restricted, #noAI is the default.

## The standing rules

| rule | what it requires |
| --- | --- |
| Crisis tripwire | Escalates to senior + sub-service on litigation / disclosure / deal / restructuring / life-safety / regulatory triggers. |
| Legal & ethical gates | Mandatory at Enterprise before the client sees the work; by exception at SME. |
| Data & AI | MNPI never enters AI tools; #noAI defaults for restricted clients; EU AI Act & GDPR aligned; CSRD anti-greenwashing enforced at the Journalist and GC personas. |
| US ↔ Europe calibration | Regional defaults for internal comms (works councils), privacy, tone, market structure and ESG. |

## The design principles this is accountable to

- **Quality lives in the system, not the person.** Every judgment is a system procedure, not the operator's call — that is what makes output operator-independent.
- **Co-pilot, not autopilot.** A named senior Strategy Owner carries accountability at four judgment gates; the engine does everything between them.
- **Reason from reputation, don't template.** Every step is grounded in UP's theory of reputation, so the output withstands scrutiny.
- **One insight, integrated.** Great communications can't be great on its own — everything flows from one human insight, orchestrated across all channels.
- **Every step makes an artifact and has a gate.** You never advance until the step's quality check passes.
- **Depth scales to the client.** An SME runs a lean version; an enterprise runs the full, governed version.
- **The engine compounds.** Every completed strategy feeds the knowledge base, so the next one starts sharper.

  "PESO shape should be earned-led for corporate reputation, supported by owned proof hubs, executive and employee channels, social content and selective paid amplification only after the route is validated."
- **fails** — Does every claim carry its proof?
  "Measurement baselines and numeric targets are not established."
- **fails** — Is the document as short as it can be while still complete?
  "Everything in line of sight: business objective → communication objective → strategic approach → messages, channels and tactics → KPIs."
- **fails** — Is every client-facing page in the reader's language — no unexplained process terms?
  "Direction. GET existing Vivacom customers WHO stayed through integrations, migrations and ordinary service frustrations TO feel that staying was a sensible and rewarding choice BY acknowledging the bumpy road and translating Vivacom's proof into visible everyday value."
- **fails** — Would you be comfortable reading it aloud to the client's board?
  "The one page everything else flows from. A gap here is a gap in the thinking."


## The wording — sentence by sentence

| requirement | rule |
| --- | --- |
| Plain words | Use the everyday word, not the impressive one. No jargon. No acronym without its meaning at first use. No filler. |
| Short sentences | One idea per sentence. Active voice. If a sentence needs a second read, rewrite it. |
| Concrete, not abstract | Say what happens, who does it, and by when. Replace vague claims with facts. |
| Proof, not adjectives | Every claim carries evidence. Delete superlatives that carry none. |
| Confident, not inflated | Assured, warm, direct. No hedging that hides a decision; no claim that outruns its proof. |
| One name per thing | Call the same thing by the same name in every document. Never rename a concept midway. |
| Reader's language, not the method's | Client-facing documents are written in the reader's language, not the method's. No process term reaches a client page unexplained. |

## The whole text — how the document reads end to end

| requirement | rule |
| --- | --- |
| One clear purpose | The reader knows in the first paragraph what this document is and what it is for. |
| Headline first | Every section starts with its point, then the support beneath it. A busy reader who reads only the headings still gets the story. |
| Logical flow | Sections follow one order of thought. Each builds on the one before. No jumps, no repeats. |
| Right length | As short as the content allows. Anything that supports but does not advance the argument goes to an appendix. |
| Visual clarity | Tables for comparisons, short lists for sequences, bold sparingly. White space is part of the writing. |
| Self-contained | A new reader can use the document without a briefing. Terms, context and next steps are inside it. |

## Who enforces it

The AI applies these rules in every draft. The human checks them at every gate. The Review Board's Journalist persona attacks unclear or inflated language. A document that fails the check goes back — it does not advance.
